node.title: Low-multiplier three-petal LS6 flats form an exact prefix ladder
node.statement: For an LS6 atom with a<=e=deg(Etilde)<=s=ell-a, Euclidean division gives an exact disjoint parametrization by quotient polynomials Q of degree e-a with fixed leading coefficient and tails R of degree at most s-e. At fixed Q, D=T_Q+R is one ordinary monic locator-prefix cell of depth ell+e-1. Over a field of order Q_0 there are exactly Q_0^(e-a) cells, and their ambient-normalized mass cancels exactly to binom(n,j)/Q_0^(ell+a-1). At e=a there is one prefix cell. This proves a ladder adapter, not maximum prefix flatness.
